transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… well, I guess I’m here because the clinic kind of got on me about how little I’ve been eating. I didn’t really think it was, like, something I needed to come talk to someone about, but they were pretty firm about it.

Most days I’m just trying to get through everything. I’ll grab coffee before I go to the warehouse, because it’s early and I’m packing stuff and moving around, and then later maybe I’ll have a yogurt or just a few bites of something after my GED class. It’s not like I’m trying to make a big deal out of it, it’s just… sitting down for a real meal feels like it messes everything up. Like it throws off the way I’m trying to keep everything in line, if that makes sense.
Are you trying to lose weight?

I mean… yeah, I guess I am, but it doesn’t feel like this big dramatic thing the way people make it sound. It’s more like… when the number goes down, I feel like I’m finally getting somewhere, like I’m doing something right for once.

And I know people keep saying stuff. Like my work pants are loose now, and people at work or whatever will say I look too thin, and it’s embarrassing because then I feel like they’re watching me. But at the same time, I don’t really see why everyone’s acting like I need to put it back on. Like, if I finally got it down, why would I want to undo that?
Are you afraid of gaining weight back?

Yeah… I mean, I guess I am. I don’t always say it like that because it sounds kind of extreme, but yeah, I get scared about it.

Like if there’s fried food in the break room at work, or if I’m at church and someone gives me this big plate and everyone’s eating, I start thinking, okay, if I eat this, is it going to show on me? Like right away. I know that probably sounds stupid, because obviously one plate doesn’t just, like, instantly change your whole body, but that’s where my mind goes. I’ll keep thinking about it after, like while I’m trying to do other stuff, and I’ll want to check the scale just to see if it did something.

It’s not even always hunger or not hunger, it’s more like… I don’t want to feel like I lost control and then suddenly I’m going backward. So yeah, gaining it back does scare me.
Have you ever eaten a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within an hour or two?

Um… I don’t really know what counts as “large,” I guess. Like, large to me might not be large to somebody else. I don’t think I’ve had one of those times where I’m just eating a ton of food nonstop for an hour or two, if that’s what you mean.

Sometimes I’ll eat more than I meant to, like if people are around and there’s food there, but then I’m mostly thinking about it afterward, like whether I overdid it. But I wouldn’t say it’s like a huge amount all at once. At least… I don’t think so.
Do you ever feel like you've lost control while eating?

I’m not sure… not really in the way people describe it, I guess. Like, I don’t feel like I’m blacking out or like I can’t stop my hand from picking up food or anything like that.

But I do get this panicky feeling if I’m eating something I didn’t plan on, or if other people are kind of pushing food on me and I don’t want to make it awkward. Then it feels like I’m not the one deciding, if that makes sense. Not like I’m eating a huge amount, more like I’m sitting there thinking, “Why did I let this happen?” or “I should’ve just said no.” And then I keep replaying it afterward.

So… I don’t know if that counts as losing control. It’s more like I feel out of control after the fact, because I ate differently than I meant to. But during it, I’m usually very aware of what I’m doing.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?

No… I don’t make myself throw up. I mean, I’ve thought about it in that scared, panicky way after eating something I didn’t want to eat, like, “I wish I could undo this,” but I don’t actually do that.

I don’t like vomiting anyway, and it’s not something I’ve used after meals. If I feel bad afterward, it’s more just sitting with it and worrying about it, not making myself sick.
Do you ever exercise excessively to burn off calories after eating?

I’m not totally sure what counts as excessive. I mean, I do think about calories after I eat, and I can get really uncomfortable just sitting there, like I should be doing something, but I don’t know if I’d say I do some extreme workout right after meals or anything.

Sometimes I’ll want to move around more, like take the long way or stay busy, because it makes me feel less anxious about having eaten. But I’m not sure if that’s the same as exercising to burn it off. I guess it’s more in my head a lot than a specific routine I could point to.
Do you find yourself thinking about your weight or body shape every day?

Yeah… pretty much every day. It’s kind of automatic at this point, like I don’t even always realize I’m doing it until I’m already checking.

Especially when I look in the mirror before class or before softball, I get stuck on certain parts of me. My stomach and my thighs are the main ones. They just look… bigger than they should, even if maybe someone else wouldn’t see it that way. I’ll stand there turning a little or pulling at my shirt, and then it’s like my whole mood for the day gets decided right there.

If they look okay enough, I feel like I’m doing good, like I can handle the day. But if they look wrong or too big, then it feels like I’m failing before I’ve even gone anywhere. And I know that probably sounds dramatic, but it really can mess with how I feel for the rest of the day.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Yeah… I mean, I guess I have. People keep saying it like it’s this big alarming thing, and my work pants have gotten loose enough that I notice it when I’m packing stuff and moving around, like I’m pulling them up more than I used to.

But it’s hard for me to see it the way other people do. Like when someone says, “You look too thin,” I don’t really… I don’t know, it doesn’t land the same. I still look at myself and feel like there’s more that needs to change.

And honestly, when the number goes down, it feels like I’m finally getting somewhere. Like all the effort is actually doing something. So when people act like I need to put it back on, I get kind of upset, because I don’t really understand why I should be pushed to undo it.
Do you think you would still be afraid of gaining weight if you couldn't see yourself in the mirror or didn't know what you weighed?

Yeah… I think I would. I mean, not knowing the number or not seeing myself would maybe make it harder to check, but I don’t think it would make the fear go away.

Like if I eat something that feels “bad” to me, like fried food from the break room, or if I’m at church and I end up with a big plate because people are serving food and watching, it’s like my mind immediately starts going, “That’s going to show on you.” Even if I haven’t looked in a mirror yet. I’ll feel scared that it’s already changing something, like it’s going to be noticeable right away, even though I guess logically food doesn’t work that fast.

And then I’ll keep thinking about it over and over, like replaying what I ate, how much it was, whether it was too much. That’s usually when I want to check the scale, because I feel like I need some kind of proof one way or the other. So even if you took away the mirror or the scale, I think I’d still be afraid. I’d probably just be stuck wondering and feeling anxious because I couldn’t check.
Do you think your weight is a problem because of how it makes you look or because of how it makes you feel physically?

I guess… more because of how it makes me look, or how I think it makes me look. Physically, I don’t really see it as this huge problem the way other people do.

Like, I know you’re worried, and people at church have made comments or acted concerned, and I’m not trying to be rude about that. I know they probably mean well. But in my head I’m still like… I’m going to work, I’m doing my classes, I’m still getting through my day and keeping up with what I need to do. So it’s hard for me to understand why everyone is making it sound so serious.

I guess if I was lying in bed all day or couldn’t do anything, then maybe I’d be like, okay, something is really wrong. But that’s not what’s happening. I’m still living my life. So when people say my weight is a problem physically, I kind of feel like they’re making it bigger than it is. I’m not saying they’re totally wrong, I just… I don’t feel it the same way they seem to see it.
Do you feel like your weight is something you can control?

Yeah… I mean, I think that’s kind of the whole thing for me, honestly. It feels like one of the few things I can keep control over.

Like I know I’m here because the clinic was getting on me about how little I’ve been eating, and I get why they’re asking, but in my head it doesn’t feel like I’m doing something extreme. It feels like I’m just keeping things in line. Most mornings before the warehouse I’ll just grab coffee, because if I sit down and eat breakfast it feels like the whole day starts wrong, like I’ve already messed up before I’ve even gotten to work.

And then by the time I’m done there, or if I have GED class, I might have a yogurt or just a few bites of something after, but a real meal feels… I don’t know, too much. Like it throws everything off. If I eat an actual full meal, then I start thinking about it for the rest of the day, like I need to fix it somehow or be more careful later.

So yes, I guess I do feel like my weight is something I can control, mostly by controlling what I let myself eat. It’s not like everything else is always easy to manage, but that part feels like something I can keep tight, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like gaining weight would mean you've lost control over your life?

Yeah… I think it would feel that way. Maybe not like my whole life, exactly, but it would feel like I failed at the one thing I’m supposed to be able to keep under control.

Like if I eat something from the break room, especially fried food, I don’t just think, “Okay, I ate that.” I start thinking right away that it’s going to show on me, like people are going to be able to tell. Or at church, if someone gives me a big plate and I feel like I can’t really say no because people are watching or being nice, I’ll eat some of it and then afterward it’s like my brain won’t let it go. I keep replaying it, like how much was on the plate, how much I actually ate, whether it was too much, whether I looked greedy or like I’d let myself go.

And then I want to check the scale because I feel like I need to know if I messed up. It’s not even always logical, because I know one meal probably doesn’t change everything right away, but it feels like it does. It feels like if the number goes up, even a little, then I didn’t hold the line, and if I can’t hold that line then… yeah, it feels like I’m losing control.
Do you feel like your body shape would be unacceptable if you gained weight?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t know if “unacceptable” sounds too harsh, but that’s kind of how it feels in my head.

Like, when I’m getting ready before class, or before softball, I’ll look in the mirror and I can get really stuck on my stomach and my thighs. Even if nothing has probably changed from the day before, they’ll look bigger than they should to me. And then it’s like that decides how I feel about myself for the whole day. If they look flatter or smaller, I feel like, okay, I’m doing good, I’m keeping things under control. But if they look bigger, or if my clothes feel a certain way, then I feel like I’ve failed before I even leave the house.

So if I gained weight, I think I’d be afraid those parts would look even more… wrong, I guess. Like they’d be too much, and people would notice. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but in the moment it doesn’t feel dramatic. It feels like proof that I messed up.
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly about not being able to control how your body looks?

Yeah… mostly, I think. It’s like I’m scared that if I gain weight, my body will change in a way I can’t hide or undo fast enough.

Like if I eat fried food from the break room, even if it’s not a huge amount, I start feeling like it’s going to show on me right away. Same thing at church if someone gives me a big plate and I eat more than I meant to. I’ll be sitting there afterward thinking about how it’s probably going to go straight to my stomach or my legs or something, and then I can’t stop thinking about whether people will notice.

And then I get this urge to check the scale, because I feel like I need proof one way or the other. I know that probably doesn’t make total sense, like logically I know one plate of food shouldn’t instantly change how I look, but it feels like it does. It feels like my body could just get away from me if I’m not watching it closely enough.
Do you feel like gaining weight would change your body shape in a way that you couldn't control?

Yeah… that’s pretty much what I’m scared of. Like if I gain weight, it feels like my body would start changing in ways I wouldn’t be able to stop, or I wouldn’t notice until it was already obvious.

It happens even with one thing, like if there’s fried food in the break room and I eat some, I don’t just think of it as that one food. I start thinking, okay, now it’s going to show on me. Like my stomach or my legs are going to look different, even if I know that probably doesn’t happen instantly. Or at church, if someone gives me a big plate and I feel like I have to eat some of it, I’ll be thinking about it afterward for the rest of the day, like how much I ate and whether it was too much.

And then I want to check the scale because I feel like I need to know if it changed something. It’s like I can’t just trust that my body is the same. I get scared that if I’m not watching it, it’ll get away from me somehow.
Is your fear of gaining weight more about not being able to fit into your current clothes or about the actual number on the scale?

I think it’s kind of both, but if I’m being honest, the scale number is the thing I go to for proof. Like the clothes matter because if something feels tight, I immediately panic a little, but then my brain wants the number to tell me if something actually changed.

Like if I eat fried food from the break room, even if it’s just a little, or if I’m at church and someone gives me a big plate and I eat more than I meant to, I start thinking it’s going to show on me right away. I’ll be sitting there replaying what I ate and wondering if it’s already going to my stomach or my legs. And then I want to check the scale, because I feel like I need to know. Like if the number is up, then it confirms I messed up, and if it’s not, then I can calm down a little… at least for a bit.

So it’s not only about fitting into clothes, I guess. It’s more like the number feels like something I can check, something exact, even though I know I probably put too much importance on it.
Is your fear of gaining weight because you believe it would make your body look unacceptable to you?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, “unacceptable” sounds kind of harsh, but that is how it feels in my head sometimes.

Like when I look in the mirror before class or before softball, I’ll focus right away on my stomach and my thighs. Even if nobody else would probably notice anything, to me they look bigger than they should, or bigger than I can stand seeing. And then it kind of sets the tone for everything after that. If they look okay, or I feel like I look smaller, I feel like I’m doing good that day, like I can handle things better. But if my stomach looks rounder or my thighs look too big, it feels like I already failed before the day even started.

So yeah, gaining weight scares me because I picture that feeling getting worse. Like I’d look in the mirror and not be able to feel okay with what I see.
Do you think gaining weight would make you feel like you're losing control over how your body looks?

Yeah… yes, that’s exactly how it feels. Like gaining weight wouldn’t just be my body changing, it would feel like I lost control of it.

It’s not even always a huge thing that starts it. Like if I eat fried food from the break room at work, even if it’s just some fries or something someone brought in, my mind doesn’t treat it like just food. I’ll start thinking, okay, now this is going to show. Like my stomach is going to look different, or my legs are going to look bigger, and I won’t be able to stop it. Same thing at church if someone gives me a big plate and I feel awkward not eating it. I’ll eat some, and then afterward I keep going over it in my head, like how much was on the plate, how much I actually ate, whether it was too much.

And then I want to check the scale, because I feel like I need to know if something changed. It’s like if I don’t check, then I’m just sitting there imagining it getting worse or showing up on me somehow. I know that probably sounds dramatic, because one meal shouldn’t instantly change how I look, but in the moment it feels really real. Like if I’m not watching it closely, my body could just get away from me.
Is your fear of gaining weight because you want to maintain a certain body shape or because you are afraid of the health consequences of being overweight?

It’s more about the body shape, I think. Not really health consequences. Like, I know people talk about health and weight and all that, but when I’m scared in the moment, that’s not what I’m thinking about.

It’s more like… if I eat something I feel I shouldn’t have, like fried food from the break room, or if I’m at church and someone gives me a big plate and I eat more than I planned, my brain goes straight to, “This is going to show.” Like I picture it showing on my stomach or my legs right away, even if I know that probably doesn’t make sense. I’ll keep thinking about it after, replaying what I ate, and then I want to check the scale because I feel like I need proof of whether something changed.

So yeah, I guess I’m afraid of not keeping the shape I’m trying to have. The health part isn’t really what scares me in those moments. It’s more the idea that my body will look different and I won’t be okay with it.
